slides.title: The August ^^curve myth^^ is costing you a test date
"August is harder because the retakers take it"
slides.body: Every July this rumor convinces students to skip the August test. The logic sounds right — ambitious seniors retaking, tougher competition, a crueler curve. It's wrong, because your SAT score never depends on who else is in the room.

slides.title: Equating is set before you ever sit down
slides.body: Your scaled score is fixed by the difficulty of the test *form*, not by the students taking it. A harder form gets a more generous conversion, an easier form a stricter one — worked out in advance. A 1400 in August equals a 1400 in March, point for point.
slides.tip: Other students' scores never touch yours

slides.title: Pick the date your prep peaks
slides.body: August is the one date where summer prep walks in fresh — no homework competing for your hours, and the September and October tests still in your pocket if you want another shot. Choose your date for *that* reason, not for a rumor.
slides.tip: Next dates after Aug 22: Sep 12, Oct 3
